comparisons.peer_topic: Foreign Exchange Hedging Strategy and Instruments
comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup hedges fair value changes from foreign exchange rate movements in available-for-sale debt securities and long-term debt denominated in non-functional currencies using forward foreign exchange contracts or cross-currency swap contracts.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C use foreign currency derivatives to hedge the fair value of available-for-sale (AFS) debt securities denominated in non-functional currencies. GS designates foreign currency forward contracts as fair value hedges for this purpose, while C uses forward foreign exchange contracts or cross-currency swap contracts. Both companies exclude forward points from the effectiveness assessment; GS notes that gains/losses on hedges relate to both spot and forward points included in market making, whereas C states changes in fair value of forward points are excluded from effectiveness assessments and reflected directly in earnings. Neither company reports a material net gain or loss for 2024, though C does not provide specific dollar amounts in the cited text while GS reports not material.

sentences.text: The firm designates certain foreign currency forward contracts as fair value hedges of the foreign exchange risk of non-U.S. government securities classified as available-for-sale.

The net gains/(losses) on hedges and the related hedged available-for-sale securities were not material for 2024, were $(2) million (reflecting a loss of $127 million related to hedges and a gain of $125 million on the related hedged available-for-sale securities) for 2023 and were $(30) million (reflecting a gain of $266 million related to hedges and a loss of $296 million on the related hedged available-for-sale securities) for 2022.

Citigroup hedges the change in fair value attributable to foreign exchange rate movements in available-for-sale debt securities and long-term debt that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency of the entity holding the securities or issuing the debt.
The hedging instrument is generally a forward foreign exchange contract or a cross-currency swap contract.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value hedge accounting for foreign currency risk
comparisons.peer_summary: Hedges of foreign currency risk on long-term debt and AFS securities are used, with gains and losses from changes in spot rates and excluded components recorded in principal transactions revenue and net interest income.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and GS both hedge foreign currency risk on AFS securities using fair value hedge accounting. JPM hedges long-term debt and AFS securities against changes in spot foreign currency rates, recording gains/losses in principal transactions revenue and net interest income. GS hedges non-U.S. government AFS securities using forward contracts, with gains/losses included in market making. Both companies exclude forward points from the spot rate effectiveness assessment; JPM records excluded components in principal transactions and net interest income, while GS includes both spot and forward points in market making.

sentences.text: The firm designates certain foreign currency forward contracts as fair value hedges of the foreign exchange risk of non-U.S. government securities classified as available-for-sale.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Investment Hedge Policy and Accounting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm uses forward foreign exchange contracts to hedge net investments in foreign operations, with gains/losses on qualifying hedges reported in AOCI and excluded forward points recorded in Interest income.
comparisons.comparison: MS uses forward foreign exchange contracts as fair value hedges, similar to GS. However, MS applies this strategy to net investments in foreign operations (reported in AOCI), whereas GS applies it to available-for-sale securities (reported in market making). Both companies exclude forward points from hedge effectiveness testing and record changes in fair value of these excluded components currently in earnings (MS: Interest income; GS: Market making).

sentences.text: The firm designates certain foreign currency forward contracts as fair value hedges of the foreign exchange risk of non-U.S. government securities classified as available-for-sale.
The gains/(losses) on the hedges (relating to both spot and forward points) and the foreign exchange gains/(losses) on the related available-for-sale securities are included in market making.
The Firm uses forward foreign exchange contracts to manage a portion of the currency exposure relating to its net investments in foreign operations.
The forward points on the hedging instruments are excluded from hedge effectiveness testing and changes in the fair value of this excluded component are recorded currently in Interest income.
